name: geosilo_encode
description:
Encode a `GEOMETRY` into the compact GEOSILO format and return a `BLOB`. With one argument, the integer scale is derived from the geometry's CRS — degrees default to `1e7` (≈1 cm), projected meters to `100` (1 cm). With two arguments, the second explicitly sets the scale. To use the result with the native GEOSILO `ST_*` overloads, cast it with `::GEOSILO`: the explicit `BLOB → GEOSILO` cast validates the silo header and fails on a bad one (`TRY_CAST` returns `NULL` instead). There is no cast from `GEOSILO` back to `BLOB`. `geosilo_decode` and `geosilo_metadata` accept the `BLOB` directly.

**DuckDB 2.0 build:** `scale` must be a positive integer — `0` or a negative scale raises an error (the Haybarn 1.5 build silently returned `POINT EMPTY` for `0`). Scaled coordinates must fit a 32-bit integer (about ±214 at `1e7`, ±21,474,836 at `100`), otherwise encoding fails with an overflow error. Z, M and ZM geometries encode and decode correctly, and the `BLOB → GEOSILO` cast validates the whole blob rather than only its header.

examples.description: Default scale (auto from CRS, or `1e7` if absent)
Explicit scale — UTM / Web Mercator data, 1 cm precision
Cast the BLOB to GEOSILO for the native `ST_*` overloads

name: geosilo_decode
description:
Decode a GEOSILO blob back into a standard `GEOMETRY`. Most callers don't need to call this directly — the implicit `GEOSILO → GEOMETRY` cast runs it on demand for any `ST_*` function that doesn't have a native GEOSILO overload (e.g. `ST_Buffer`, `ST_Union`, `ST_AsText`).

**DuckDB 2.0 build:** Every read is bounds-checked: a truncated or corrupt blob raises an `Invalid Input Error` instead of crashing the process, and nesting deeper than 16 levels is rejected. Use [`try_geosilo_decode`](#try_geosilo_decode) to get `NULL` instead of an error, or [`geosilo_is_valid`](#geosilo_is_valid) to filter untrusted blobs first.

examples.description: Round-trip a polygon through the encoding

name: geosilo_metadata
description:
Read a GEOSILO blob's header **without decoding the geometry**. Returns `STRUCT(geometry_type VARCHAR, vertex_type VARCHAR, scale BIGINT)`. Useful for filtering by geometry type or auditing the integer scale of a stored column before any heavy spatial work.

**DuckDB 2.0 build:** The header is fully validated (magic byte, version, geometry and vertex type, positive scale); an empty or malformed blob raises an error, and a `NULL` input gives a `NULL` struct whose fields are also `NULL`.

examples.description: Inspect the header of stored silo blobs

name: geosilo_is_valid
description: **DuckDB 2.0 build only.** Returns `TRUE` when the value is a structurally valid GEOSILO blob — a known header, element counts consistent with the data, nesting of at most 16 levels and no trailing bytes — and `FALSE` otherwise. It never raises an error for malformed input, so use it to filter untrusted `BLOB`s (from files, other systems or user input) before decoding them. Accepts `GEOSILO` or `BLOB`; `NULL` gives `NULL`.

examples.description: A valid blob and a corrupt one

name: geosilo_validate
description: **DuckDB 2.0 build only.** Validates a GEOSILO blob and returns `NULL` when it is valid, otherwise a message describing the first problem found — truncated data, a bad magic byte, an unsupported version, an element count larger than the data, excessive nesting or trailing bytes. Use it to report why a blob is rejected. Accepts `GEOSILO` or `BLOB`.

examples.code:
SELECT b, geosilo_validate(b) AS problem
FROM (VALUES (geosilo_encode(ST_Point(1, 2))), ('\x47\x01'::BLOB), ('\x54\xff\xff\xff\x7f'::BLOB)) t(b);

name: try_geosilo_decode
description: **DuckDB 2.0 build only.** Decodes a GEOSILO blob into a `GEOMETRY` like [`geosilo_decode`](#geosilo_decode), but returns `NULL` instead of raising an error when the blob is malformed. Accepts `GEOSILO` or `BLOB`.

examples.description: Decode a column that may contain corrupt values
examples.code:
SELECT ST_AsText(try_geosilo_decode(b)) AS wkt
FROM (VALUES (geosilo_encode(ST_Point(1, 2))), ('\x54\xff'::BLOB)) t(b);

name: ST_GeometryType
description: Native GEOSILO overload — returns the geometry type (e.g. `POINT`, `POLYGON`) by reading a single byte of the silo header. No WKB decode.

examples.description: Geometry type of a GEOSILO value

name: ST_IsEmpty
description: Native GEOSILO overload — `TRUE` if the encoded geometry has no vertices, including polygons, multi-geometries and collections made only of empty parts (`GEOMETRYCOLLECTION(POINT EMPTY)` is empty).

name: ST_NPoints
description:
Native GEOSILO overload — total vertex count, walking the encoded geometry: every ring and sub-geometry is counted, polygon rings include their closing vertex (as in WKB), and empty points count as 0. Matches spatial's `ST_NPoints`.

**DuckDB 2.0 build:** `MULTI*` geometries and `GEOMETRYCOLLECTION`s are counted correctly (the Haybarn 1.5 build returns `0` for them and `1` for `POINT EMPTY`).

name: ST_X
description:
Native GEOSILO overload — X coordinate of a POINT, read straight from the silo bytes without materializing a `GEOMETRY`. Returns `NULL` for `POINT EMPTY` and raises an error for any other geometry type, like spatial's `ST_X`.

**DuckDB 2.0 build:** `POINT EMPTY` gives `NULL` (the Haybarn 1.5 build returns `NaN`).

name: ST_Y
description:
Native GEOSILO overload — Y coordinate of a POINT, read straight from the silo bytes without materializing a `GEOMETRY`. Returns `NULL` for `POINT EMPTY` and raises an error for any other geometry type, like spatial's `ST_Y`.

**DuckDB 2.0 build:** `POINT EMPTY` gives `NULL` (the Haybarn 1.5 build returns `NaN`).

name: ST_XMin
description:
Native GEOSILO overload — minimum X across the geometry, computed by walking the integer delta stream. Pair with `ST_XMax` / `ST_YMin` / `ST_YMax` for native bounding-box prefilters. Returns `NULL` for an empty geometry.

**DuckDB 2.0 build:** empty geometries return `NULL` instead of `NaN`, and coordinates on both sides of the antimeridian are handled exactly.

name: ST_XMax
description:
Native GEOSILO overload — maximum X across the geometry. Walks the integer delta stream; no WKB decode. Returns `NULL` for an empty geometry.

**DuckDB 2.0 build:** empty geometries return `NULL` instead of `NaN`, and coordinates on both sides of the antimeridian are handled exactly.

name: ST_YMin
description:
Native GEOSILO overload — minimum Y across the geometry. Walks the integer delta stream; no WKB decode. Returns `NULL` for an empty geometry.

**DuckDB 2.0 build:** empty geometries return `NULL` instead of `NaN`, and coordinates on both sides of the antimeridian are handled exactly.

name: ST_YMax
description:
Native GEOSILO overload — maximum Y across the geometry. Walks the integer delta stream; no WKB decode. Returns `NULL` for an empty geometry.

**DuckDB 2.0 build:** empty geometries return `NULL` instead of `NaN`, and coordinates on both sides of the antimeridian are handled exactly.

name: ST_Area
description:
Native GEOSILO overload — planar area of the polygonal parts, computed with the [shoelace formula](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shoelace_formula) directly on the integer coordinates rebuilt from the delta stream (no WKB decode). Each polygon contributes its exterior ring minus its holes regardless of ring orientation; `MULTIPOLYGON`s and polygons inside a `GEOMETRYCOLLECTION` are summed; points and linestrings contribute `0`. Matches spatial's `ST_Area`.

**DuckDB 2.0 build:** linestrings return `0` and holes are always subtracted (the Haybarn 1.5 build returns a non-zero area for a closed `LINESTRING` and mis-handles holes wound in the same direction as the shell); the sum is accumulated in double precision so large polygons at scale `1e7` cannot overflow.

examples.description: A hole is subtracted whichever way it is wound

name: ST_Length
description:
Native GEOSILO overload — total planar length of the linear parts (`LINESTRING`, `MULTILINESTRING`, and linestrings inside a `GEOMETRYCOLLECTION`), computed on the integer delta stream without rehydrating a `GEOMETRY`. Polygons and points return `0` — use [`ST_Perimeter`](#st_perimeter) for polygon boundaries. Matches spatial's `ST_Length`.

**DuckDB 2.0 build:** polygons return `0` (the Haybarn 1.5 build returns their perimeter), and segments that cross the antimeridian are measured correctly: `LINESTRING(-179 0, 179 0)` has length `358`.

examples.description: Segments spanning the full longitude range

name: ST_Perimeter
description:
Native GEOSILO overload — perimeter of the polygonal parts, summed over every ring (holes included), computed on the integer delta stream without rehydrating a `GEOMETRY`. Points and linestrings return `0`. Matches spatial's `ST_Perimeter`.

**DuckDB 2.0 build:** linestrings return `0`, and linestrings inside a `GEOMETRYCOLLECTION` are no longer added to the perimeter.
